text:
Jay was away on a school trip to the museum, and he was worried about his grandmother. He typed to his phone assistant: remind gran to take her blue pill at six, but don't call her and don't use a loud alarm. She hates loud noises.
The assistant understood that Jay wanted a quiet reminder only. It set a soft chime on gran's tablet for six o'clock, with a note that said, Time for your blue pill. It did not place any call, and it did not turn on the loud alarm.
Jay loved how easy it was. At six, gran tapped the note, took her pill, and sent him a smiley face.

A radio plays stations that send out news, music and talk. People use it to hear the weather in the morning or a match at night. What they change most often is the station and the volume. Someone who wants frequent news updates might say, Put on the news station, or Turn it down a little. Some small radios run on a battery, so people ask, Did you charge the radio? Many people listen while they eat breakfast and take a vitamin. Smart radios can also save favourite stations, so you can say, Play my usual station, instead of looking for the number.

A robot mower cuts the grass by itself, so nobody has to push a mower on Saturday. It stays inside a wire or a map line, and it goes back to its base when the battery is low. People change when it works, how short the grass should be, and which part of the garden it skips. They say things like, Cut the grass a bit shorter, Don't mow when it rains, or Leave the far corner alone. Sprinklers work in a similar way. You point the spray at the dry patch and say, Water the front lawn for ten minutes. If a fork or a toy is left on the grass, the mower may stop, so pick things up first.

They want to know when a film is showing at the cinema.
What time is the film on?
When does the new space movie start?
Showtimes for tonight, please.
I'm making dinner and I'll heat some creamy pasta first, so tell me when the film begins.
Remind me what's showing at the cinema tomorrow at seven.
Any good films on this weekend?
Could you check the cinema and tell me the times for the funny one with the dog?
Is there a late show?
I'd love to see something after work, so what is playing and when?

Person: I'm chopping onions in the kitchen and the music is too quiet. Turn it up.
Assistant: Which speaker should I turn up, the kitchen one or the living room one?
Person: The kitchen one. But I don't want it so loud that it hurts my ears.
Assistant: Okay. I turned the kitchen speaker up to level six.
Person: Good. Can you tell me about the traffic on my way to school? It looks stormy outside.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't check live traffic from this speaker. I can tell you the weather, though. There is heavy rain until noon.
Person: Then I'll take an umbrella. Thanks!

A smart bulb is a light you can control with your voice. It is for making a room feel right: bright for reading, soft for the evening. Most bulbs can change their brightness and their colour, so a lamp can convert from plain white to warm yellow or even blue. People say things like, Make the lamp dimmer, Turn the bedroom light to warm, or Set the hall light to silver white. After a late ride home on the bus, someone might just say, Lights on. And before bed, Turn everything off. Short words like these are all the bulb needs.

name: grocery_list_update
does: Adds an item to the shopping list, with how many you want, like a fancy cheese or a basil bush from the garden shop.
inputs: the item and how many of it, if the person says
people say:
- We're out of eggs.
- Put two lemons on my list.
- Don't let me forget the fancy olive oil.
- I need a bush of fresh basil for Sunday.
- Write down oat milk, the big one.

An air conditioner takes the warm air out of a room and blows cool air back in. People use it on hot days so they can sleep, work or just feel calm. A fan does not make the air colder, but moving air feels cooler on your skin. Many fans hang from the ceiling and have three speeds. What people change is the temperature, the speed and the time it stays on. They say, It's too hot in here, Make it a bit cooler, or Switch it off at midnight. Heat can give you a headache, even on a cloudy day, so a cool room helps.

name: outfit_weather_check
does: Looks at the forecast for a place and a day and says what to wear.
inputs: the place and the day, or right now if the person says nothing
people say:
- Will I need a coat this morning?
- Is that silver sky going to bring rain?
- When will the rain begin?
- Should I sweep the porch with the broom today or wait for the wind to stop?
- Is it warm enough for shorts in Leeds on Friday?

name: call_for_help
does: Calls a person or the emergency number and tells them where you are and what is wrong.
inputs: who to call and what happened, if the person says
people say:
- There is smoke coming from the pan!
- Get my sister on the phone, I fell.
- A large tree just came down on our road.
- Call someone now, and keep trying until they answer.
- Get the fire brigade, it's the kitchen.

A phone call lets two people talk even when they are far apart. You press a name and the phone rings. If nobody picks up, you can leave a voicemail, and the person hears it later. Missed calls show up as a number on the screen. People change how loud the call is, whether it uses speakerphone, and who they call. They say, Call Dad, Put it on speaker, or Call back the last number. A rough line or a weak signal can break up the sound, so people say, Say that again, or Call me back. If you ride a bike or a horse, you may ask for speakerphone so your hands stay free.

Reading time is a few quiet minutes with a book, often before bed. A bookmark keeps your place so you can find the chapter again. Many people read a chapter a night, and some like a timer that tells them when to stop. A new book may arrive in the mailbox, and people look forward to it. What they change is the book, the page, the size of the letters and how long they read. They say, Open my book at chapter four, Read for thirty minutes, or Make the letters bigger. A safe, calm routine helps some people dream well afterward.

A workout is a set of exercises done in order, like squats, push-ups and a short run. Each exercise has sets and reps: a rep is one movement, and a set is a group of reps. Rest days let the body get strong again. People change the length, the exercises and the number of reps. They say, Make the workout shorter, Do ten more squats, or Skip today, I need a rest day. They may also ask to filter the list so it shows arm exercises only. Every person has a different plan, and some people start a new one on their birthday for a fresh start.

Moving house means taking your things to a new home. People pack boxes, write labels, tell the post office their new address and set up water, power and internet. Movers carry the heavy items. What people change is the date, the address and what goes in each box. They say, Book the movers for Saturday instead, Change my address, or Put a note on this box that says kitchen. Dusty old boxes can make you sneeze, so it helps to wipe them. Some towns have free boxes you can pick up. A warm sweater is good to keep in the last box you close.

name: show_countdown
does: Calculates how long it is until a show starts on a channel and tells you.
inputs: the show or the channel name
people say:
- How long until the news?
- When is the show with the gray wolf on?
- Is the match from my city on tonight?
- Will I miss the start if I make tea?
- What time is the quiz on channel five?

They want to know what two numbers make when they are put together.
What is 20 plus 10?
Twenty and ten, total?
Sum of 7 and 8?
How much is 45 and 15 together?
What do I get if I put 9 with 6?
Can you tell me what 300 plus 250 comes to? It's for my favourite recipe, and I want to cook for more people.
Sorry to bother you, but I'm buying plants for my balcony after last week's flood washed the old ones away, so could you please tell me what 18 plus 27 comes to?
Quick one: 100 and 1?
Bring 12 and 12 together for me.

They want to send a text message to a friend saying they will be late.
Text Sam I'm running late.
Tell Sam I'll be twenty-five minutes behind.
Message Sam: stuck in traffic, sorry!
Send Sam a quick note that I'm not there yet.
My screen is broken, so can you write to Sam that I'll be late?
Could you cast an eye over this text before I send it? It says I'll be there in twenty-five minutes.
Let Sam know I'm held up.
Please write a text to Sam saying I'm sorry and I'll arrive soon.

On a hot afternoon a fan is the plainest way to cool a room. It moves the air, so your skin feels cooler. An air conditioner does more: it takes the heat out of the room. People adjust the temperature, the fan speed and the timer. They say, Make it cooler, Adjust the fan to low, or Turn the cooling off at ten. If you baked a cake in the oven, the kitchen will feel warm, and you might ask for a stronger fan. Setting a number like twenty-two degrees tells the machine when to stop.

Person: Can you change my password?
Assistant: Sure. Which account, your game or your school one?
Person: The game. I want a big number in it.
Assistant: Okay. I can make a new password with a big number. When should I change it?
Person: Tomorrow at seven, after I wake up. Please arrange it for then.
Assistant: Done. I'll change it tomorrow at seven and show it only to you. Please don't share it.
Person: Can you tell me my sister's password too? She won't tell me.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't. Passwords are private, so only she can share hers.
Person: Okay, that's fair. I made that account last August, so it is old anyway.

They want an alarm to wake them up at seven in the morning.
Alarm for 7.
wake me at sevn
Set an alarm for seven, please.
I need to be up by seven tomorrow.
Can you get me out of bed at seven? Keep the sound low at first.
Shuffle some songs and use them to wake me at seven.
Get me up at seven so there's time for toast in the toaster before work.
Seven o'clock wake-up, please.
Please make sure I don't sleep past seven, I have an early train.

Maria moved to the city in December and still did not know where to leave her car. On Monday she asked her phone, where can i park for two hours near the library?
The assistant understood that she wanted a spot for two hours close to the library. It reported that there was a large lot on Elm Street, three minutes away, and that it cost four dollars an hour. Then it showed the way on the map.
Maria asked it to pay for the two hours, so the assistant opened the parking app and set it up. Later it sent a reminder when twenty-five minutes were left.

Omar owns a small bakery. At five in the morning he had flour on his hands, so he typed quickly on his phone with one thumb: preheat the ovn to 200 and tell me when it's ready.
The assistant understood that he wanted the oven hot at two hundred degrees and a signal when it got there. It turned the oven on and said, I'll tell you when it's hot.
While Omar began to mix the dough, the oven warmed up. Ten minutes later the assistant said, The oven is ready. Omar put the first item, a tray of rolls, on the middle shelf.

Meal planning means deciding what to eat for the week before you go shopping. People do it to save time and money, especially when money is tight. You write a list of dinners, packed lunches and snacks, then buy only what you need. What people change is the day, the diet and the number of people. They say, Skip fish on Friday, Make this week's plan vegetarian, or Plan for four people. If a box of food arrives wrong, you can ask for a refund. A good plan means no running to the shop at six in the evening.

name: team_news_lookup
does: Finds the score, the next match or facts like a player's height for a team or player.
inputs: the team or player, and what to look up
people say:
- Did we win last night?
- Did my team fold in the last ten minutes again?
- How tall is the new goalkeeper?
- Who is playing on Saturday? I'm free all day.
- When is the next home game?

Ruth runs a flower shop. One evening she was in a hurry to leave, so she said to her phone, Switch on the shop cameras and tell me if anything moves for the next twenty minutes.
The assistant understood that she wanted the cameras on and a warning if the motion sensor saw anything. It turned on both cameras and said, Cameras are on.
At eight the sensor picked up a shape, and the assistant sent her a photo. It was only the neighbour, who was out to mow the grass behind the shop, seen through the thick glass door. Ruth laughed, then asked the assistant to play her evening playlist on the way home.

Person: Mute it.
Assistant: Sure. Do you mean your phone or the blue tablet?
Person: The tablet.
Assistant: Done. The blue tablet is muted. Do you want it to stay muted until morning?
Person: Yes. I'm making oatmeal and the kids are asleep.
Assistant: Okay, it will stay quiet until seven.

Mr Hall, a retired teacher, heard a noise on the road outside his house. He said to his smart speaker, Turn on the porch light and show me the front camera.
The assistant understood that he wanted two things: the porch light on and the front door camera on the screen. The light began to glow, and the picture appeared on his tablet. He could see the road, the bins and a cat.
Mr Hall smiled. Since he was awake now, he asked the assistant to read the local news. It read three short stories and then stopped.

When you buy something online, a package travels from a shop to your door. The tracking page shows where it is: packed, shipped, out for delivery. People use it to know when to be home. If you click on the wrong colour with your mouse, you can often cancel before the shop closes the order. A soft parcel, like a pillow, may be left by the door. What people change is the delivery day, the address and the time. They say, Where is my package, Send it to my office, or I want a refund.

Tina runs a small cafe. She had just unplugged the old fridge to clean it, and her hands were wet and cold, so she typed in a hurry: put heavy cream and two dozen eggs on the shopping lsit, and send john a message that we are out of milk.
The assistant understood two jobs. It added heavy cream and twenty-four eggs to the shopping list. Then it sent John a message that said, We are out of milk.
It told Tina both things were done. She dried her hands and went back to the fridge.

Dana, a busy parent, put the laptop on the floor near the socket and said to it, Restart the computer and open the folder called school forms.
The assistant understood that she wanted two things: a restart, and then the folder. It restarted the laptop. After the plain blue screen came up, it opened the school forms folder and showed three files.
While Dana filled in the first form, the assistant tracked the battery and told her it was at eighty percent, so she did not need to move. She thanked it and went on with her work.

Mr Wilson was not good with technology. The remote had too many buttons. So he spoke to the television, Take me straight to channel twenty-five, please.
The assistant understood that he wanted channel twenty-five. It switched there. A show about an old train route was on, and Mr Wilson liked it.
Then he said, I don't want the grandchildren to change the channel. Can you lock it? The assistant turned on the children's lock, so the channel could only be changed with a code. It told him the code in a clear voice and said he could ask to unlock it any time.

Lily was eight. One night the smoke alarm began to beep in the hall. She said to the family speaker, Call Grandpa. Then she stopped. No, call Mom!
The assistant understood that Lily had changed her mind. It did not call Grandpa. It called Mom and said that Lily was at home and the alarm was beeping.
Mom said it was probably a low battery, and she told Lily to write a note on the fridge to buy a new one. The assistant gave one tip: if you ever smell smoke, go outside and wait. Lily wrote the note, and it was the correct thing to do.

name: music_room_mover
does: Moves the music from one speaker to another room, so you can keep listening as you walk around.
inputs: where the music is now and where it should go
people say:
- Bring the song into the kitchen.
- I have gloves on, so send the radio to the garage speaker.
- Make the bedroom silent and play it in the hall.
- Take this to the other room.
- Follow me upstairs.

A birthday is the day each year when a person gets one year older. People use their phones to remember dates, pick gifts and send cards. A good reminder comes weekly in the month before, so there is time to shop. People change the date, the gift idea and how much they want to spend. They say, Remind me about Ben's birthday, Find a gift under twenty dollars, or Send a card. Some gifts are food, like a cake they can eat together, and a gift card for fuel works well for a driver.

name: wellness_check_call
does: Calls an older person at a set time and asks how they feel, then tells the family if they do not answer.
inputs: the person's name and the time
people say:
- Ring Grandpa at nine and see if he's okay.
- Dad sneezed all day, so check on him tonight.
- Tell me if Mum doesn't pick up.
- Check on Mrs Lee, the owner of the corner shop, every morning.
- Is the check-in call working?

A robot vacuum cleans the floor by itself. People set a schedule so it runs while they are out. It goes back to its base when the battery is low. What people change is the time, the room and how strongly it cleans. They say, Clean the kitchen now, Try the bedroom first, or Don't run when I'm home. If a pile of letters from the mailbox is on the floor, pick it up first. When the dust bin is full, the robot may say so. A low hum is normal.

They want to listen to the news on the radio.
Put the news on.
I'm sick in bed and can't reach the radio. Could you play the news?
What is happening in the world today?
Radio news, please.
I want to hear the headlines while I look for my wallet.
It's too quiet in here. Turn on the news station.
I need to pay some bills and want something on in the background, so tune to the news.
I haven't heard today's news yet.
Switch to the news channel, please, if it's not too much trouble.

Priya was a busy parent with a toddler asleep on her shoulder. Very softly she said to her phone, Could you please turn off the hourly alerts from the photo app, because every buzz wakes the baby and I really need her to sleep?
The assistant understood that she wanted the hourly notifications switched off. It turned them off and said, Done. The photo app will not buzz anymore.
The last buzz had been a like on a picture of the baby in her yellow dress. Priya whispered thanks and asked it to play soft music.

Ken, an office worker, came home that evening to the smell of fresh paint from the next flat. He told his speaker, Run the air purifier tomorrow at seven, and keep it on low.
The assistant understood that Ken wanted the purifier to start at seven the next morning at a low speed. It set the schedule and said, The purifier will start tomorrow at seven on low.
Ken looked at the purifier. Its small light was dim, which meant it was waiting. He opened a window for a few minutes and went to bed.

name: car_status_check
does: Updates you on the fuel level and the tyre pressure of the car.
inputs: which car, if there is more than one
people say:
- Do I have enough fuel for Saturday's drive?
- Is the car ready for a short trip to the shops?
- Are my tyres okay?
- How much petrol is left?
- Is anything wrong with the car?

Grandpa Leo was walking his dog Max, with the leash wrapped around his arm, when he remembered the recipe. He said to his phone, print my chicken recipe, but not in colour, and don't print the pictures.
The assistant understood that he wanted only the words, in black and white. It sent the recipe to the printer at home.
When Leo got back, the page was waiting on the tray. The recipe serves six. Max, who was hungry, sat down by the kitchen table and waited too.

name: bin_sorter
does: Says which bin an item goes in and when that bin is collected.
inputs: the item and the street or address
people say:
- Where does a banana peel go?
- Is a pizza box paper or rubbish?
- When should I bring the green bin out?
- I need to be careful with this broken glass, where does it go?
- Which day is garden waste?

name: speaker_volume_match
does: Matches the volume of several speakers so there is no difference between rooms, either for a temporary party or for good.
inputs: which speakers, and for how long
people say:
- I just plugged in a new speaker, make it as loud as the others.
- The patio is too quiet compared to the kitchen.
- Make everything the same level just for the party.
- Fix the sound, the hall is much louder.
- Even them out for tonight.

Person: Send the report to my team.
Assistant: Which report? You have two in your drafts.
Person: The one from May.
Assistant: Got it. It is a heavy file with a lot of pictures. Do you want me to send it as it is?
Person: Can you make it half the size?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't make a file smaller. I can send a link instead, and the team can open it online.
Person: Okay, send a link.
Assistant: Done. The link went to your team.

Person: Turn down the brightness and set a reminder for my medicine.
Assistant: I can do both. What time should the reminder ring?
Person: My usual time.
Assistant: I don't know your usual time yet. Is it morning or evening?
Person: Evening, around eight. I rest on the bench after supper.
Assistant: Okay. I set the reminder for eight every evening and lowered the brightness.
Person: Thanks.

Mrs Ortiz was not good with technology. She was about to travel, and she stood in her garden after cooking beef stew, just to breathe the cool air. She said to her tablet, Could you please water the tomatoes on the left side every morning while I am away, because I don't want them to dry out?
The assistant understood that she wanted the sprinkler on the left bed to run each morning while she was gone. It set it for six every morning, and it told her in plain words what it had done.
Mrs Ortiz said thank you, as if she were talking to a person.

They want to know how many days are left until a certain date.
How many days until Sunday?
Days left until the egg hunt at Easter?
Count the days to my holiday, please.
How long until tomorrow at seven, in hours?
Sorry, but I've got a cough and the doctor said to come back in two weeks. What date is that?
How many sleeps till Christmas?
Tell me how many days I have left before the party on the fifth.
What's the countdown to my birthday?

Person: Clean the air.
Assistant: Do you mean in your car or at home?
Person: In my car. I read a news story about smoke and the air smells bad.
Assistant: I can't control the air in your car, I'm sorry. But I can remind you to open the windows when you stop.
Person: Okay. Remind me in twenty-five minutes.
Assistant: Done. I'll show it on the digital screen too.
Person: Can you whisper it? The baby is asleep in the back.
Assistant: Yes, I'll say it in a whisper.

name: ride_log_summary
does: Tracks a bike ride and tells you the distance, speed and time.
inputs: which ride, or the last one if the person says nothing
people say:
- How far did I go today?
- What was my speed on the hill?
- Did I ride longer than last week?
- I ate a seed bar halfway, so how long was I out?
- How far did I get before I was tired?

Zoe was on a school trip, walking up a frozen path by the lake. Her feet were cold and she wanted to know how far she had gone. She typed to her phone, Count steps.
The assistant understood that she wanted her step count. It said, You have walked 4,200 steps so far, which is about three kilometres.
Zoe typed again, Watch pace. The assistant said it would watch her pace and tell her if she went too slowly to reach the bus on time. Ten minutes later it said, You are going a little slow. Zoe laughed and walked faster.
